title.title: Chromatic splitting fails at height three
title.subtitle: Claim: for $p \ge 5$ Hopkins's strong chromatic splitting fails at height 3, seen by a nonzero map on $\pi_{-3}$

plain: The sphere's layers were predicted to overlap in a simple way; at the third layer, they don't

object.heading: Strong chromatic splitting, by height and prime (schematically)
object.caption: rows: height $n = 1, 2, 3$ · columns: $p = 2, 3, 5, 7$ · blank: not covered here

beats.text: The prediction: adjacent chromatic layers of the sphere overlap in a simple wedge
True at heights 1 and 2 for $p > 2$; Beaudry broke the strong form at $n = p = 2$
Claimed: it fails at height 3 for every $p \ge 5$

steps: The prediction holds at heights 1 and 2
At height 3, a natural map would have to vanish on the predicted pieces
It does not vanish on the real sphere, so the prediction fails

achievement.label: Hopkins's chromatic splitting conjecture, strong form
achievement.context: So it fails even as an equivalence of $E(2)$-local spectra. Before: Beaudry (2017) at $n = p = 2$
achievement.note: Positive side: a $2^n$-stage filtration holds for $p > n + 1$

verify.detail: Manuscript only: five papers, 372 pages, mixed positive and negative results
verify.ourCheck: We read the proof outline; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Layers of the sphere should overlap simply. True at heights one and two.
At height three, a map that should vanish on the prediction does not.
Claimed: it fails for every prime from five.

sources.quote: (i) For p >= 5 the canonical map L_0 L_{K(3)}S -> L_0 L_{K(2)} L_{K(3)}S is nonzero on pi_{-3}, so Hopkins's strong chromatic splitting fails at height 3 even as an equivalence of E(2)-local spectra.
known true at heights 1 and 2 for p > 2 (Shimomura-Yabe, Hopkins); Beaudry (Geom. Topol. 2017) disproved the strong form at n = p = 2.
(iii) Positive: for n >= 1, p > n+1, L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p admits a 2^n-stage filtration with the predicted cofibers
Five papers, 372 pages; mixed positive and negative results.
